title: A separable polynomial quotient over an algebraically closed field is a product of copies of the field
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $P\in F[T]$ be monic and separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial] of degree $n$, and let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field containing $F$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Write $R=\Omega[T]/(P)$, where coefficients are mapped from $F$ to $\Omega$. Then evaluation at the $n$ distinct roots of $P$ induces an $\Omega$-algebra isomorphism $R\cong\prod_{\rho\in\Omega,\,P(\rho)=0}\Omega$; the root set has exactly $n$ elements.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field), separable polynomial case; Chinese-remainder factorization over an algebraically closed field

proof.text: By [lem-pc-separable-polynomial-distinct-roots-alg-closed], the image of $P$ in $\Omega[T]$ factors as $\prod_{P(\rho)=0}(T-\rho)$, where the roots $\rho$ are pairwise distinct and their set has exactly $n$ elements.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00U3, separable polynomial case

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-polynomial-quotient-distinct-linear-crt] to this product of pairwise distinct linear factors. The Chinese-remainder map sends the class of $f(T)$ to $(f(\rho))_{P(\rho)=0}$ and is an $\Omega$-algebra isomorphism from $R=\Omega[T]/(P)$ to the product of one copy of $\Omega$ for each root.
The factor index set in the preceding step is exactly $\{\rho\in\Omega\mid P(\rho)=0\}$, and step 1 gives its cardinality as $n$; hence this is the asserted evaluation isomorphism and root count.
